title: The wire: forge types
description: Part of the source of every type on the wire (#1135, #5380): one file per domain in Packages/Wire/schema. A $ref to another file names it (core.schema.json#/definitions/JSONValue); scripts/wire.sh gen reads them all.

ForgeAction.description: A write or a read that an item's page offers (#4329, #4361): forge/comment, forge/label, forge/close (a close, a reopen or a transition; closeNotPlanned is a close with reason not_planned, where the forge has it, #4404), forge/merge (now, or with auto), forge/approve, forge/rerun, forge/log, forge/diff, forge/add-child, forge/blocked-by, forge/assign (#4403), forge/cancel-auto-merge and forge/ready (#4410).

ForgeAddChildRequest.description: forge/add-child (#3271): add a child to an epic's plan: a new issue (title, with level story, task, spike or bug) or one that is there (issue: #12, owner/repo#12, its URL, or a Linear key such as ENG-4). A new child gets the level's label and the epic's feature: label. GitHub and Linear.

ForgeApproveRequest.description: forge/approve (#3130): approve a pull request at sha, the head commit its page shows (refused when the head moved).

ForgeAssignRequest.description: forge/assign (#4403): people to assign to an issue or a pull request, and people to take off it, by their login on the forge. At most 10 of each at once.

ForgeBlockedByRequest.description: forge/blocked-by (#3271): the issues that block a child of a plan, to add and to take off, by node. GitHub and Linear.

ForgeBoards.description: forge/boards (#3282): the boards of the projects of this machine's folders, each once, by url, in its project's order.

ForgeBoardsRequest.description: forge/boards (#3282): the boards of every folder's project on this machine, or of one folder's.

ForgeCapabilities.description: What one forge on a list's page fills (#4329, #4361), so a client hides what it does not: issues and pulls say it has them; labelColors that its labels have a #rrggbb colour; avatars that its items have authorAvatar; stateReason that its closed issues have stateReason. createdAt that its items have createdAt, and closedAt that its closed and merged items have closedAt; children, linkedPulls and events that an item's read has them (#4373); total that it counts a list's items, for ForgeList.total (#4396); releases that it has releases, for forge/releases and forge/release (#4426); a pull request's fields (#4409): branches that it has headRef and baseRef, mergedBy and mergeCommit that a merged one says them, size that its read has additions, deletions and commits, reviewers and closes that its read has them, and checkTimes that its checks have startedAt and finishedAt; each is absent from an earlier daemon, which has none. commentCount says how to read ForgeItem.comments: exact; capped at commentsMost (show 50+ there); or detail, only on an item's own page (hide it on the row).

ForgeCheck.description: One of a pull request's checks (#3129): a check run or a commit status. state is passing, failing, running or skipped; url is its page on the forge. startedAt and finishedAt are when it started and ended (#4409), where the forge says them (ForgeCapabilities.checkTimes): absent on a check that has not started, and finishedAt on one still running; a commit status has neither.

ForgeCloseReason.description: Why forge/close closes an issue (#4404): completed, or not_planned where the forge has it (the action closeNotPlanned).

ForgeCloseRequest.description: forge/close (#3130): close an issue or a pull request, or with reopen open it again; with transition, move a Jira issue by that transition of its workflow, by its id from the page's transitions (#3260). reason is why an issue closes (#4404): completed (the default) or not_planned, which only an issue whose actions have closeNotPlanned takes; refused with reopen or a transition, and on a pull request.

ForgeComment.description: A comment on an issue or a pull request (#3129), as Markdown. bot says a bot or an app wrote it. avatar is the author's picture, a URL that only forge/image reads (#4363); none when the forge gives none.

ForgeCommentCount.description: How a forge counts an item's comments (#4329): exact; capped at the forge's commentsMost (Linear's 50); or detail, only on an item's own page (Bitbucket issues, Azure Repos), so a list's count is 0.

ForgeCommentRequest.description: forge/comment (#3130): a comment, as Markdown, on an issue or a pull request, as the person whose machine it is.

ForgeDiff.description: forge/diff (#3130): a pull request's changed files at its head, as the app's own diff draws them (#1341); cut says some files are listed with no hunks; url is its files on the forge.

ForgeDiffFile.description: One file a pull request changes (#3130): change is added, removed, modified or renamed; note says why it has no hunks, when it has none.

ForgeDiffHunk.description: One @@ block of a file's diff (#3130).

ForgeDone.description: What a forge write did (#3130): url is the comment or the item on the forge; auto says a merge waits for the checks; reran is how many runs or pipelines were run again.

ForgeEvent.description: One event on an issue's timeline (#4373), as its forge says it: kind is what happened; actor is who did it, absent when the forge says nobody (a deleted account); label is the label that labelled and unlabelled name; assignee is the person that assigned and unassigned name; source is the issue or pull request that referenced names, or the pull request that closed closed it with.

ForgeEventKind.description: What happened on an issue (#4373): a label was added or removed, a person assigned or unassigned, it closed or reopened, or another issue or pull request named it.

ForgeFeature.description: A feature (#3267): name is its label's after feature:, with the label's colour where the forge gives one; epics counts its epics, open the open ones. issues counts its open issues that are not epics, of the newest 500 open issues (#3741); a feature with no open epic and no such issue is finished. refs are the lineage refs of its open issues and open epics, waiting the ones labelled alex-todo, and updatedAt the newest update of any of them (#4115), so a client finds the sessions labelled #<n> for them and which wait for Alex.

ForgeFeatures.description: forge/features (#3267): the feature:<name> labels of the epics (the issues labelled epic, open or closed, the newest 500), by name; approvals are the lineage refs of the newest 100 open pull requests labelled needs-approval (#4115), so a client finds the sessions labelled P#<n> for them; errors says a forge that could not be read, as in ForgeList.

ForgeFeaturesRequest.description: forge/features (#3267): the features of every folder on this machine, or of one folder's repo.

board.description: A board's url, from forge/boards (#3282): only the epics on that board.

ForgeImage.description: forge/image (#4009): an image's bytes, so that a client never loads a forge page's remote URL. mimeType is image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif or image/webp, read from the bytes.

ForgeImageRequest.description: forge/image (#4009): the url of an image on a forge page. Only a forge's own image hosts are read (for GitHub: github.com's user-attachments and repo assets, and user-images, private-user-images, raw and avatars on githubusercontent.com); the forge's token goes only to its own hosts.

ForgeItem.description: An issue or a pull request (a GitLab merge request) as its forge says it (#3129): one model for GitHub, GitLab, Linear and Jira (#3260), so one page draws each. node is its lineage node (kind issue or pr, ref github:issue:alexec/agents#12). state is open, closed or merged; status is the tracker's own name for its step, where its workflow has steps (a Jira status, as In Progress; one in Jira's Done category is closed). folder is a folder on this machine on its repo, to act from. labels have their #rrggbb colour where the forge gives one (#2956). The pull request's own fields: draft; checks is passing, failing, running or none; review is approved, changes_requested or review_required; mergeable is mergeable, conflicting or unknown; autoMerge says auto-merge is on. The hierarchy (#3267): parent is the issue it is a sub-issue (a Linear or GitLab child) of; level is epic, story, task or spike, from its labels; feature is the name of its feature:<name> label; progress is a parent's closed children of all of them, where the forge says it: in a GitHub list, and on an issue's own read. standing says it has the label standing: a standing epic, whose plan is a query (#3659). authorAvatar is the author's picture, a URL that only forge/image reads (#4363), where the forge gives one (ForgeCapabilities.avatars). stateReason is why a closed issue closed (#4365): completed, not_planned or duplicate, where the forge says it (ForgeCapabilities.stateReason); absent on an open issue and on a pull request. createdAt is when it opened and closedAt when it closed or merged (#4373), where the forge says them (ForgeCapabilities.createdAt and closedAt); closedAt is absent while it is open. A pull request's branches (#4409): headRef is the branch it merges from and baseRef the one it merges into, where the forge says them (ForgeCapabilities.branches); on its own read at least, and on a list's row where the list says them. A merged pull request's mergedBy is who merged it and mergeCommit the commit it made on baseRef (ForgeCapabilities.mergedBy and mergeCommit); each is absent while it is open or closed unmerged.

ForgeItemDetail.description: forge/issue and forge/pull (#3129): one item with its body (Markdown) and a page of its comments, the newest page first and at most 50, oldest first in the page; cursor is the page before it, absent at the first comment. A pull request's checks, review threads (line comments, in threads) and files changed come with it. head is a pull request's head commit, which forge/merge and forge/approve name (#3130); mergeMethods are the ways its repo allows, the repo's default first; start is the new-agent form for an issue. transitions are the moves an issue's workflow allows now (Jira, #3260), which forge/close takes in place of a close or a reopen. actions are what the item's page offers now, from its forge and its state (#4361): a merged pull request has no merge and no reopen, a closed item no close; absent from an earlier daemon, when the page shows what it did before. On an issue's read (#4373), where the forge says them (ForgeCapabilities): children are its sub-issues, linkedPulls the pull requests that close it, and events its timeline, oldest first (labelled, assigned, closed, referenced and the like); each is absent where the forge gives none. On a pull request's read (#4409), where the forge says them (ForgeCapabilities): additions, deletions and commits are its size; reviewers are the people asked to review it and the people who reviewed it, each once with their newest state; closes are the issues it closes when it merges.

ForgeItemRequest.description: forge/issue and forge/pull (#3129): the item's lineage node, and for an older page of its comments the cursor of the page after it.

ForgeLabel.description: A label on an issue or a pull request (#3129), with its #rrggbb colour where the forge gives one (#2956).

ForgeLabelRequest.description: forge/label (#3130): labels to add to an issue or a pull request, and labels to take off it, by name.

ForgeLabels.description: forge/labels (#3130): the labels an issue or a pull request can have, at most 100, by name.

ForgeLead.description: An epic's lead session (#3267): its id, title and state.

ForgeLinked.description: An item that an issue's read names (#4373): a sub-issue, or a pull request that closes it; or an issue that a pull request closes (#4409). state is open, closed or merged, as ForgeItem.state.

ForgeList.description: forge/issues and forge/pulls (#3129): a page of items, the last updated first. cursor is the next page, absent at the end. errors says a forge that could not be read (not connected, a rate limit), and the items of the others still come. forges says what each forge on the page fills (#4361); absent from an earlier daemon. total is how many items the whole list has, the sum of each forge's count, kept from each forge's first page (#4396); absent when a forge on the list gives no count (ForgeCapabilities.total) or could not be read, and from an earlier daemon.

ForgeListError.description: A forge forge/issues or forge/pulls could not read (#3129): forge is github, gitlab or linear.

ForgeListRequest.description: forge/issues and forge/pulls (#3129): the issues or pull requests of every folder on this machine, or of one folder's repo. state is open (when not said), closed or all; a closed pull request includes a merged one. label, assignee (a login) and query (words in the title or body) narrow the list. limit is 1 to 100, 50 when not said; cursor is the last page's. feature (a name: work for the label feature:work) narrows it to one feature's items (#3267). board (a board's url, from forge/boards) narrows it to one board's items (#3282).

ForgeLog.description: forge/log (#3130): the last lines of each failed check's log, as plain text.

ForgeLogRequest.description: forge/log (#3130): the end of a pull request's failed checks' logs, or of one check by name.

ForgeLogins.description: people/setForgeLogins (#2951): the caller's own GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Jira (#3313), Forgejo (#3836), Bitbucket and Azure DevOps (#3853) logins, for Settings ▸ You, replacing what was kept; blank clears one.

ForgeMergeMethod.description: How forge/merge merges a pull request (#3130): a merge commit, one squashed commit, or its commits rebased onto the base.

ForgeMergeRequest.description: forge/merge (#3130): merge a pull request at sha, the head commit its page shows (refused when the head moved), by method (the repo's default when absent); with auto, the forge merges it once its checks pass.

ForgeNodeRequest.description: forge/labels, forge/rerun and forge/diff (#3130): the issue or pull request.

ForgePlan.description: forge/plan (#3267): an epic and its plan. children are its sub-issues (at most 100), step by step, in the forge's order within a step. steps are the children of each step, the first first. lead is the session on this machine, not archived, that works on the epic in lineage (its label #<n>, or the Linear key) and is labelled lead. standing is set only for a standing epic (#3661): its children are then the open issues of its query, not its sub-issues, at most 100, in order (priority, then the oldest), all in one step 1; its item has no progress.

ForgePlanChild.description: A child of an epic in forge/plan (#3267). blockedBy are the issues it is blocked by, open or closed, in the plan or not. step is 1 for a child that no other child blocks, else one more than the last step of the children that block it; a blocker outside the plan adds no step, and children in a loop share the step after the rest. blockedOutside are its open blockers outside the plan (an issue of another epic). A forge with no dependencies (GitLab Free) puts every child in step 1.

ForgePlanRequest.description: forge/plan (#3267): the epic's lineage node, an issue on GitHub, GitLab or Linear.

ForgePlanStep.description: A step of a plan (#3267): its number, from 1, and its children's nodes.

ForgeProgress.description: A parent issue's children (#3267): done are closed, of total.

ForgeRelease.description: A release on a forge (#4426). node is its lineage node (kind release, ref <forge>:<repo>/release/<tag>), which forge/release reads and lineage keys its cost by. repo is the repo as the forge names it, and folder a folder on it. latest is the repo's newest published release that is neither a draft nor a pre-release. publishedAt is absent on a draft; author and authorAvatar when the forge says them; assets is how many files it has.

ForgeReleaseDetail.description: forge/release (#4426): a release, the release before it (previous, its tag; absent for the first), how many commits are between the two (commits, at most what the forge's compare gives) and the pull requests they merged, from each squash commit's (#n) or (!n), oldest first. compareUrl is the forge's page of the range.

ForgeReleasePull.description: A pull request in a release (#4426): its node, its number, and its title as its squash commit says it, with the (#n) taken off; sha is the commit.

ForgeReleaseRequest.description: forge/release (#4426): a release's lineage node, as ForgeRelease.node says it.

ForgeReleases.description: forge/releases (#4426): the releases of the folders' repos, newest first (a draft, which has no publishedAt, by createdAt). none are the forges in reach that have no releases, and why, so a client says so (Linear and Jira have no releases); errors are the forges that could not be read.

ForgeReleasesRequest.description: forge/releases (#4426): the releases of every folder's repo on this machine, or of one folder's, at most limit (1 to 100, 30 when absent) of each repo.

ForgeReviewer.description: A reviewer of a pull request (#4409): login is who; avatar their picture, a URL that only forge/image reads, where the forge gives one; state is their newest review, or pending while they are asked and have not answered, or were asked again since.

ForgeReviewerState.description: A reviewer's state (#4409): approved, changes_requested, commented (reviewed with no verdict) or pending (asked, not answered).

ForgeStanding.description: A standing epic's query (#3659, #3661), as the daemon read it from the standing block in the epic's body. labels: the issue has all of them; any: at least one of them; not: none of them; milestone: none, any or a milestone's name; parent: none, only issues that are no other issue's sub-issue (#4335, #4348). lanes is how many lanes its lead runs at once, 1 when the block does not say. error says why there is no query: no block, a second block, or an unknown or bad field; with an error, the plan has no children.

ForgeStart.description: The new-agent form for an issue (#3130, Start Agent), as a view's agents/start-agent fills it (#834): the prompt, the session's labels, and a new worktree's name.

ForgeTransition.description: A move an issue's workflow allows now (#3260): its id, which forge/close takes, and its name, as Start Progress. category is the status category it goes to: new, indeterminate or done.

ProviderForget.description: providers/forget (#3398): the provider was removed; its machine ends its server and deletes its secrets.

RequestForge.description: The forge item a request is (spec 3862 §4).

checklist.description: An issue's lines under its first "## What <name> does" heading.

screenshots.description: A pull request's image links under its "## Screenshots" heading.

updatedAt.description: The item's, when it was last read: a newer one is read again.

seenAt.description: The last sweep that saw it open with the label.

ReviewDismissRequest.description: reviews/dismiss (#3330): a person's Dismiss on a pull request in the sidebar's For Review. The host keeps it, so that pull request is not listed again.

url.description: The pull request's page, as its ReviewPull says it.

ReviewOpenRequest.description: reviews/open (#3464): a person opened a pull request's page from the sidebar's For Review. The host keeps it, so its row is drawn read on every client.

url.description: The pull request's page, as its ReviewPull says it.

ReviewPull.description: An open pull request labelled needs-approval, a UI change waiting for the person (#2811), in the sidebar's For Review (#3330) until it is labelled approved or changes-wanted, is closed, or is dismissed.

ref.description: Its lineage ref, "github:owner/name#12" or "gitlab:group/project!12": a press opens its Work page in the app. Nil from an older host: a press opens its forge page.

opened.description: The person has opened its page (reviews/open, #3464): its row is drawn read, not bold.
